models.name: Aspire 14 AI
models.notes: A device tree written from owners' hardware reports, sharing almost everything with the Aspire 16's. An owner started Omarchy's edge live image on it in November 2026, and it picked this tree and reached the installer. Nobody has installed it yet.

models.name: Aspire 16 AI
models.notes: A device tree written from owners' hardware reports. An owner booted it on Ubuntu's live USB in November 2026, with the screen, keyboard, disk, USB, battery and Bluetooth working. Wi-Fi needs a board file copied from Windows, since linux-firmware has none for its card.

models.name: Vivobook 14
models.notes: Owners boot it with the X Plus Vivobook S 15's device tree or a patched Zenbook A14 one.

models.name: Vivobook S 15
models.notes: The maker download on the firmware page has the X Elite model's files only. ASUS sells both chips as S5507QA, so which package carries the X Plus model's signed files isn't clear yet.

reports.note: Two owners report the screen going dark after the boot menu on the RC image.

models.name: Vivobook S16 (S3607QA)
models.notes: A device tree written from two owners' hardware reports, in an OLED and an LCD version. An owner booted the OLED version on Ubuntu's live USB in November 2026, with the screen, keyboard, touchpad, Bluetooth, USB, HDMI and disk working. Wi-Fi needs board data that linux-firmware doesn't have yet.

models.name: Zenbook 14 (2026)
models.notes: The device tree builds on the Zenbook A14 UX3407QA's and isn't posted to the kernel lists yet. The hardware IDs are proposed in ubuntu/stubble#96 and the ACPI tables in aarch64-laptops/build#178.

reports.note: The stock 4.5.0rc1 image shows a black screen and resets, since it has no device tree for this model. With the device tree and patches from omarchy-pkgs #1634 and an owner's board package, it installs and runs on linux-omarchy 7.3.

models.name: Ascent QN10
models.notes: A draft device tree, written from its ACPI tables on the Zenbook A16's, whose firmware describes the same power, USB and PCIe wiring. Nobody has booted it yet. Ethernet and HDMI are the likeliest gaps.

reports.note: The screen goes dark after install since the image moved to Omarchy's own kernel.

models.name: XPS Googlebook
models.notes: Its Android device name is mica. The community tree is adapted from the HP Googlebook 14's, with the Dell wiring taken from the stock tree in Google's recovery image. It leaves the internal drive off, so it only runs from USB for now.

reports.note: Boots into the Omarchy desktop from USB, on Linux 7.2 with a device tree written for it, started from the unlocked bootloader's boot-from-external-drive menu. The backlight stays very dim, Wi-Fi doesn't come up yet, and the internal drive is left off.

models.name: MagicBook Art 14
models.notes: Honor's driver download has no compute DSP firmware, so those two files still come from the laptop's own Windows.

models.name: Googlebook 14
models.notes: A community tree runs mainline Linux from the second boot slot and leaves Googlebook OS on the first. Nearly everything works, with kernel patches for the keyboard, the audio DSP and suspend. The internal mics click now and then, and battery time estimates come out about 8 times too short.

models.name: OmniBook 5 16
models.notes: It shares the OmniBook 5 14's board, and Omarchy's kernel gives it that laptop's device tree.

models.name: ProBook 4 G1q
models.notes: Owners report Ubuntu booting on it with the X Plus OmniBook X 14's device tree.

reports.note: Installs from the edge channel's nightly image and reaches the desktop, but the screen stays dark at the disk password prompt. Loading the USB-C display drivers before the disk is unlocked brings the prompt up; that fix isn't in Omarchy yet.

models.notes: Its out-of-tree device tree is the Glymur reference board's with fixes for this machine, and keeps the reference board's compatible.
